reports.title: RALPH LAUREN REPORTS SECOND QUARTER FISCAL 2027 RESULTS AHEAD OF EXPECTATIONS AND RAISES FISCAL 2027 OUTLOOK

lines: In the second quarter of Fiscal 2027, the Company had an effective tax rate of approximately 20% on a reported basis and 19% on an adjusted basis, in-line with its outlook.

For Fiscal 2027, the Company expects constant currency revenues to increase mid- to high-single digits to last year on a 52-week comparable basis, now centered around 6% to 7%, up from a range of 5% to 6% previously, reflecting better-than-expected second quarter results.
For the third quarter, the Company expects revenues to grow approximately low- to mid-single digits on a constant currency basis, centered around 3% to 4%.
The Company's full year Fiscal 2027 tax rate is still expected to be in the range of approximately 21% to 22%.
The third quarter tax rate is expected to be approximately 23% to 24%.
The Company continues to expect capital expenditures for Fiscal 2027 of approximately 4% to 5% of revenue.

desk.headline: Revenue up 9% to $2.19bn and adjusted EPS $4.64 beats $4.27 estimate; full-year outlook raised again
results: Revenue rose 9% to $2.19bn (10% at constant currency), with every region growing: Asia +28%, North America +6%, Europe +1%.
China sales jumped more than 35%; average prices in own stores and online rose 9% on strong full-price selling.
Adjusted EPS rose 22% to $4.64. GAAP EPS of $4.87 includes an $82m refund of US tariffs, partly used for $33m of charitable donations.
Adjusted gross margin widened to 70.5% and adjusted operating margin to 15.7%, despite higher marketing spend.
Cash and short-term investments were $1.8bn; $500m of shares were bought back this fiscal year, completing the year's plan.

guidance.summary: Ralph Lauren now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 6–7% at constant currency (was 5–6%) and operating margin to widen by 80–100 bp (was 60–80 bp). Q3 revenue is expected to grow 3–4%.

points: Management said its core shoppers remain resilient in all key markets, with bigger baskets and less sensitivity to price.
Europe was weaker, with lower store traffic and more discounting; the Europe outlook was trimmed while North America and Asia were raised.
Price growth is expected to slow to mid-single digits in Q3 as the company laps an 18% jump last holiday season.
The outlook assumes US tariffs near 10% through December, then a return to higher rates in Q4; tariff refunds are left out of adjusted results.
Holiday media spend is up 23% and full-year marketing is now seen at about 8–8.5% of sales.
call.source: Earnings call transcript — The Motley Fool, 5 Nov 2026; FashionUnited, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Holiday-quarter sales against the 3–4% growth guide, and whether price gains hold up.
The effect of US tariffs returning to higher rates in fiscal Q4.
Whether Europe's weaker store traffic and heavier discounting spread.
